subject: general
question: Which plant tissue is mostly found in the husk of a coconut, and what is its main function?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sclerenchyma – providing strength and rigidity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **husk of a coconut** is made up of **sclerenchymatous tissue**. This tissue consists of **dead cells** that are long and narrow, with cell walls heavily thickened due to the deposition of **lignin**.
 
• **Statement A (Collenchyma – providing flexibility)**: This is incorrect. **Collenchyma** is characterized by living cells that are elongated and irregularly thickened at the corners. Its primary function is to provide **flexibility** and **mechanical support**, allowing plant parts like stems and leaves to bend without breaking. *Hence, statement A is incorrect.*
 
• **Statement B (Sclerenchyma – providing strength and rigidity)**: This is correct. **Sclerenchyma** tissue makes the plant part **hard and stiff**. In a coconut, the fibrous **mesocarp** (husk) is composed of these fibers to provide **protection and structural integrity**. *Hence, statement B is correct.*
 
• **Statement C (Parenchyma – storage of food)**: This is incorrect. **Parenchyma** is a simple permanent tissue consisting of relatively unspecialized cells with thin primary walls. Its main functions include **photosynthesis**, **storage of food**, and providing basic support. *Hence, statement C is incorrect.*
 
• **Statement D (Xylem – conducting water and minerals)**: This is incorrect. **Xylem** is a **complex permanent tissue**, not a simple tissue like the others. It is responsible for the **unidirectional transport** of **water and minerals** from the roots to the leaves. *Hence, statement D is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Plant Tissues**: Plant tissues are broadly divided into **Meristematic tissues** (capable of cell division) and **Permanent tissues** (cells that have lost the ability to divide). Permanent tissues are further divided into **Simple** (one type of cell) and **Complex** (multiple types of cells).
 
• **Simple Permanent Tissues**:
 
 
• **Parenchyma**: Found in the soft parts of plants; can be **Chlorenchyma** (for photosynthesis) or **Aerenchyma** (providing buoyancy in aquatic plants).
 
• **Collenchyma**: Located in the **leaf stalks** (petioles) and below the **epidermis** of dicot stems. It provides **tensile strength**.
 
• **Sclerenchyma**: Provides **rigidity**. Cells are dead at maturity and lack **protoplasm**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Composition**: The cell walls of **Sclerenchyma** are thickened with **lignin**, a complex **organic polymer** that acts as a waterproof binder. This makes the tissue extremely tough and resistant to environmental degradation, which is why **coconut coir** is used in industrial applications like **ropes and mats**.
 
• **Complex Permanent Tissues**:
 
 
• **Xylem**: Composed of **tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma, and xylem fibers**.
 
• **Phloem**: Composed of **sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibers**; it transports **food (sucrose)** from leaves to other parts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lignification**: The process of **lignification** in sclerenchyma cells is so intense that the **internal space (lumen)** of the cell often disappears, leaving a solid **mechanical structure**.
 
• **Biological Significance**: In the **coconut (Cocos nucifera)**, the thick sclerenchymatous husk allows the fruit to **float in seawater** for long distances and protects the embryo from **mechanical damage** during its journey across oceans.
 
• **Types of Sclerenchyma**: It exists in two forms: **Fibers** (long, needle-like cells) and **Sclereids** (short, gritty cells found in the pulp of **pears** or the shells of **walnuts**). The coconut husk is primarily composed of **Sclerenchyma fibers**.
